title: Your World Cup, Your Daal: A Desi Food Guide to FIFA 2026's Host Cities
excerpt: As the biggest football tournament in history kicks off across North America, here is where NRIs can find a taste of home between the matches.
body:
The FIFA World Cup 2026 kicked off on June 11 with Mexico defeating South Africa 2-0 at Mexico City Stadium, inaugurating the largest tournament in football history: 48 teams, 104 matches, three countries, and 16 host cities stretching from Guadalajara to Toronto. For the millions of Indian-Americans and desi football fans scattered across the United States, Canada, and Mexico, the next five weeks promise a carnival of late-night matches, neighbourhood watch parties, and — if past World Cups are any guide — an urgent, recurring need for proper food.

India may not have qualified for the tournament (yet), but the diaspora's enthusiasm for the beautiful game has never been in question. Here is where to fuel up in and around the host cities.

## The Big Three: New York, Los Angeles, Dallas

**MetLife Stadium, New Jersey** hosts some of the tournament's marquee fixtures, including the final on July 19. The surrounding New York metro area is arguably the richest Indian food corridor in America, with Edison and Jersey City's "Little India" strips offering everything from dosa counters to chaat houses within a short drive of the stadium. In Manhattan, Michelin-starred Junoon and the newly opened Indienne in Hudson Yards set the fine-dining bar.

**SoFi Stadium, Los Angeles** sits in Inglewood, a short drive from Artesia's Pioneer Boulevard — Southern California's unofficial Little India, packed with biryani joints, sweet shops, and grocery stores. Cali Chilli, helmed by Michelin-starred chef Manjunath Mural, offers Indian-fusion in both Long Beach and Downtown LA for fans seeking something inventive.

**AT&T Stadium, Dallas** puts fans within reach of the Irving-Richardson-Plano corridor, where the North Texas desi food scene has exploded in recent years with South Indian tiffin rooms, Hyderabadi biryani specialists, and Indo-Chinese takeaway counters.

## Canada Steps Up: Toronto and Vancouver

**BMO Field, Toronto** is surrounded by one of the largest South Asian food ecosystems outside the subcontinent. Gerrard Street East — once dubbed "Little India" before the community dispersed — still anchors the scene, but the real action has moved to Brampton and Scarborough, where Punjabi dhabas, Gujarati thali houses, and Sri Lankan Tamil restaurants operate at a density that rivals neighbourhoods in Mumbai.

**BC Place, Vancouver** offers proximity to Main Street's "Punjabi Market," one of the oldest South Asian commercial districts in North America. Surrey, just across the Fraser River, is home to a thriving Punjabi food scene where butter chicken, tandoori, and chole bhature are as commonplace as dim sum.

## The Undercard Cities

**Lincoln Financial Field, Philadelphia** may not have the Indian restaurant density of New York or LA, but University City and the Northeast corridor host several reliable options. The city's South Asian grocery stores — concentrated along Bustleton Avenue — make it easy for fans hosting watch parties to stock up on samosas, pakoras, and chai supplies.

**NRG Stadium, Houston** anchors a city whose Mahatma Gandhi District (formerly Hillcroft Avenue) is one of the most vibrant desi food corridors in the American South, with Indo-Pakistani, Bangladeshi, and Sri Lankan restaurants lining the strip.

**Levi's Stadium, San Francisco Bay Area** is home territory for the largest concentration of Indian tech workers in America, and the food scene reflects it. Sunnyvale, Fremont, and Milpitas offer an embarrassment of South Indian, Gujarati, and Punjabi riches — from vada pav to pav bhaji to elaborate weekend brunch thalis.

## The Watch Party Playbook

For the millions of NRIs who will watch from home rather than the stadium, the World Cup is as much a culinary event as a sporting one. Community WhatsApp groups are already buzzing with plans for tandoori-and-football Sundays, biryani pot-luck screenings, and chai-fuelled all-nighters for the late kickoffs from Mexico.

Indian grocery chains like Patel Brothers, India Bazaar, and Apna Bazaar have begun stocking World Cup snack packs and party trays in metro areas, recognising that the desi sports-viewing occasion is evolving from a family-room affair to a community event.

## What's Next

The group stages run through June 28, with matches across all 16 venues. For the diaspora, the real action may be less about which team wins and more about which city's desi food scene rises to the occasion. With the final at MetLife on July 19 — in the heart of Indian America's densest food corridor — the beautiful game and beautiful food have never been closer.
